newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: A'dam Exchanges see structurally higher turnover.
newsitem.headline: A'dam Exchanges see structurally higher turnover.

text.p: The Amsterdam Exchanges expect trading volumes to have reached a structurally higher level, chairman George Moeller said in a New Year's speech.

Moeller, head of the newly merged Amsterdam Stock Exchange and the European Options Exchange (EOE), said share prices had risen to a historic high in 1996 but added this was not the only factor behind surging trade volumes.

"Interest (among the public) in shares is still growing, the exchanges' access...is easier than before, the cost structure has improved and the general transparency of bourse trading has grown substantially," Moeller said.
The previously announced launch of the New Market Amsterdam (NMA), a market for shares in young and promising companies, will take place in the first quarter of this year.
Moeller said the Amsterdam Stock Exchange's current trading system would be evaluated in the course of 1997.

The Exchange's departing chairman Boudewijn van Ittersum said cost cuts and strong growth had enabled his bourse to refund another 14 million guilders to its members for the financial year 1996, the same amount as in 1995.

The Amsterdam Stock Exchange's formal owner, the Dutch Association for Securities Trading, which will be disbanded this year now that the merger with the EOE has taken effect, has a shareholders' equity of about 240 million guilders. This will also be paid out to the bourse's members.
Van Ittersum said the total amount of new shares floated and issued on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange had surged by 36 percent to 32 billion guilders in 1996.
Although the volume of bond issues by the Dutch state halved in 1996, a total of 89 billion guilders in Dutch bonds was issued last year, only slightly below 1995's 91.4 billion.
